question: For a couple under 35 years old, how long do they usually try to conceive through unprotected sex before doctors consider it infertility?
explanation: You've got this! Doctors look at a full 12 months of regular, unprotected sex as the standard timeline before testing for fertility issues. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why do doctors shorten the fertility testing timeline to just 6 months for women who are 35 or older?

options.A: Increased insurance coverage for fertility testing
options.B: Faster spread of sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Higher rates of voluntary childlessness in this group
options.D: Age-related decline in egg quality and reserve

explanation: Spot on! Because egg quality and number naturally start dropping faster after age 35, checking things a bit earlier helps protect their chances of starting a family. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h1)

question: Which of these everyday lifestyle habits can negatively impact fertility in both men and women?
explanation: Brilliant! Smoking is a habit patients can actually change, and it directly hurts both sperm quality and ovarian health. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: How does being severely underweight most often lead to fertility challenges in women?

options.A: By destroying existing ovarian follicles immediately
options.B: By halting ovulation through hypothalamic suppression
options.C: By causing physical blockage of the fallopian tubes
options.D: By thickening the cervical mucus permanently

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Extremely low body fat confuses the brain's hormone signals, which pauses the menstrual cycle and stops the release of eggs. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: Which two common sexually transmitted infections are most often linked to blocked or damaged fallopian tubes?
explanation: Spot on! These two bacterial infections love to travel upward into the reproductive tract and cause scarring. Knowing this helps you educate patients better! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h3)

question: A young female patient is treated for chlamydia. What crucial step must you take as a nurse to prevent the infection from coming back?

options.A: Advise her to avoid all physical exercise for six months
options.B: Schedule immediate surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.C: Ensure her sexual partners are also evaluated and treated
options.D: Prescribe long-term daily hormonal contraceptive pills

explanation: You nailed it! Treating partners stops the back-and-forth spread of infection and keeps your patient safe from repeated pelvic inflammation. Great clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why can frequent exposure to high scrotal heat, like hot baths or saunas, lower a man's fertility?

options.A: It interferes with normal sperm production and development
options.B: It destroys the prostate gland and seminal vesicles
options.C: It blocks the release of testosterone from the adrenal glands
options.D: It causes permanent scarring of the vas deferens tubes

explanation: Fantastic! Sperm need a cozy spot slightly cooler than normal body temperature to grow properly, so extra heat disrupts the whole process. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h4)

question: Which of these options is NOT a workplace hazard that threatens reproductive health?

options.A: Working around sources of ionizing radiation
options.D: Prolonged exposure to heavy metals like lead

explanation: Easy peasy! Pasteurized milk is a healthy drink, not a toxic workplace chemical. Keep flying through these questions—you've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h4)

question: What are the main hormonal signs that point toward Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?

options.B: Permanent closure of the cervical os

explanation: Spot on! PCOS usually brings higher levels of male hormones along with unpredictable or missing ovulation cycles. You are learning clinical concepts like a pro! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: How does endometriosis commonly lead to fertility challenges in women?

options.A: By causing pelvic adhesions and tubal distortion from chronic inflammation
options.B: By completely stopping the production of progesterone in the ovaries
options.C: By thickening the inner lining of the vagina to prevent sperm entry
options.D: By accelerating the natural aging of eggs within the follicles

explanation: You got it! When tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus, it causes inflammation and scarring that can trap eggs or block tubes. Excellent work! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is the main goal when you counsel patients on reproductive health and lifestyle choices?

options.A: To force patients to follow strict medical schedules without input
options.B: To diagnose complex endocrinological disorders independently
options.C: To prescribe fertility drugs directly in community clinics
options.D: To empower patients with knowledge to make protective health choices

explanation: Brilliant! Good nursing is all about education and teamwork so patients feel confident protecting their own health. You're going to be an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h6)

question: A patient feels nervous and ashamed talking about past sexual partners during a clinic visit. What is the best way to handle this as a nurse?

options.A: Scold the patient for engaging in risky behaviors that threaten health
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to build trust and offer education
options.C: Refuse to discuss the topic further until a physician enters the room
options.D: Document the behavior as non-compliant in the permanent hospital record

explanation: You're a natural! Creating a safe, warm space builds trust and makes it easy for patients to share and learn. Keep up the daily habit—you're doing great! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h6)
